name: Iogi
tagline: Shinjuku in 29 minutes and Shibuya in 39 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Suginami City, where Seibu run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 39 minutes to Otemachi, 29 minutes to Shinjuku, 39 minutes to Shibuya and 60 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 42.4 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 6.5 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 42.4 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 42.4 m to 48.9 m, a difference of 6.5 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 3 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 2 clinics and 4 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 成瀬医院, about 20 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 荻窪病院, about 21 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Seibu Shinjuku Line.
congestion: Seibu Shinjuku Line runs at 148% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 下落合→高田馬場, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. 1LDK ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 2LDK ¥170,000 to ¥180,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

neighbours.lead: Iogi is ahead on how easy the shopping is, and little else separates the two.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Iogi. It is served by the same lines as Iogi. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. On how easy the shopping is, Iogi comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For the number of places to eat out, Kami-Igusa; for how close the centre is, Iogi.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Iogi in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Iogi. To Shinjuku, for instance, Kami-Igusa takes 3 minutes longer. On the number of places to eat out, Kami-Igusa comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 8 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Seibu Shinjuku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
